newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Holiday mode affects trading on Cyprus bourse.
newsitem.headline: Holiday mode affects trading on Cyprus bourse.

text.p: Cyprus stocks closed 1.3 percent lower this week mainly affected by the Easter lull which dominated the market, traders said.

The Cyprus Stock Exchange (CSE) general price index closed at 78.12 points on Friday from 79.14 on April 24, dropping 1.3 percent or 1.02 points. The market was closed last Friday for the Greek Orthodox Easter holidays.
"It is a little early to tell where the market is going because it is just after the Easter holidays. People are still in a holiday mood," said one trader.
Laiki Investments, a subsidiary of the Cyprus Popular Bank said short and medium term moving averages suggest the market is in bearish territory.
"Technical indicators suggest an upward movement of the market," said Stelios Markoulis from Laiki.
He said the market PE ratio is 18.5 times, rising after the price increases of March and April. In February the PE ratio was estimated at around 16 times.
This week the market was closed on Monday for the Greek Orthodox Easter and on Thursday, labour day.
Some 21 million pounds ($41.25 million) worth of government bonds made their debut on the bourse on Wednesday.
The bonds closed at 101.05 pounds on Friday on a volume of 1,000 compared to Wednesday's closing price of 100.80 pounds. There was no trading recorded on Wednesday.
The bank index, the strongest on the bourse, closed 1.24 percent lower to settle at 87.20 points.

Bank of Cyprus shares closed at 324.5, four cents lower than the closing price on April 26. The Cyprus Popular Bank ex final dividend closed at 303.5 from 308.5 last week. Hellenic Bank closing price for its fully paid shares on Friday was 291.5, dropping half a cent from April 26, while the Universal Savings Bank closed at 192.5, steady on last week.
The insurance index was lower by 0.45 percent to 59.40 and commercial companies registered declines of 2.37 percent.
Keo, the Cyprus beer and wine company, was trading at 103.5, down half a cent from its closing price last week.
Vassiliko Cement shares were trading two cents lower at 167.5 on heavy volume which represented 12 percent of trading on the bourse on Friday.
National carrier Cyprus Airways was trading at 27.7 cents on Friday from 28.3 cents on April 26.

On April 30 the company, hard hit by a decline in passenger levels and rising fuel prices last year, reported preliminary pre-tax losses of 2.13 million pounds for 1996, compared to pre-tax profits of 5.03 million pounds in 1995. (=0.508 pounds)
